- When sentiment is positive (≥0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast peak at 1.2x prior high.
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.25), model underestimates; adjust downward by 3–7% to align with mean reversion toward recent 10–15 day average.
- Forecast horizon >15 days shows persistent lag; add 1–2 days of smoothing or decay factor to reduce over-optimistic tail behavior.
- When sentiment is rising (e.g., 0.25–0.33), model tends to overreact; apply downward bias to later forecast days to avoid “sentiment-driven overcorrection.”
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 75), model should not forecast >75 unless sentiment strongly supports; cap forecasts at 75–80% of recent high.
